mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES stops falling and begins to firm, commuting-linked daytime spending recovers first and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. This mechanism predicts a positive retail response even if parks and transit stay depressed, because workplace attendance is the primary demand shifter.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -51.1 to -48.6 across the snapshot while RETAIL_REC stayed around -55 to -56
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES holding above its prior 4-week average.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility above baseline indicates more time spent near home and stronger neighborhood substitution, which suppresses retail outings within one week. The claim is falsified if higher RESIDENTIAL is followed by a stable or rising RETAIL_REC instead of a decline.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed positive at 13-14 points while RETAIL_REC remained deeply negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not drop within 7 days after RESIDENTIAL rises above 12 points and stays elevated.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT recovers by at least 3 points from its prior weekly mean, retail access and discretionary trips expand with a lag of two weeks, pushing RETAIL_REC upward. The effect fails when transit improves but workplaces and grocery-pharmacy remain weak, indicating that mobility gains are not broad enough to translate into shopping demand.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was roughly stable near -52 to -53 in the snapshot
failure_condition: A week-on-week transit improvement of 3 points or more is not followed by higher RETAIL_REC within the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: A joint rebound in GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES signals normalized out-of-home routines and bundled errand chains, which raises retail visits over the next four weeks. This interaction matters because grocery trips create nearby discretionary spillovers only when workplace mobility is also recovering.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both remained well below baseline but moved unevenly across the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days when GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both improve from their current 4-week levels.

mechanism_narrative: A recovery in PARKS mobility above its recent trough signals favorable weather or leisure-season demand, which diverts foot traffic into shared outings and supports nearby retail within two weeks. The sign flips if parks rise because indoor retail is being displaced by outdoor substitution rather than complemented by it.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points from the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rebounded from -40.9 to -27.9 and then fell again to -40.9 in the snapshot
failure_condition: A parks rebound of 5 points or more is not followed by higher RETAIL_REC within 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening restrictions, simultaneous declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES reduce cross-district movement and cut retail demand over the following month. The mechanism requires both proxies to weaken together; isolated movement in only one series is insufficient to depress retail systematically.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall below their 2-week averages
evidence_refs: fact:both series remain around -50 or worse in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall over the next 28 days when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are below their 2-week averages.

mechanism_narrative: A week-over-week drop in RESIDENTIAL below its recent positive plateau indicates people are spending more time out of home, which should lift retail almost immediately through spontaneous shopping trips. This is a short-horizon signal and fails if the residential decline reflects only measurement noise while retail remains unchanged.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 1 point week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL moved between 13.0 and 14.3 over the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher in the following week after RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 1 point.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM remains less negative than RETAIL_REC by at least 20 points, essential-trip traffic is active enough to spill into discretionary purchases, but only after a four-week lag. The hypothesis is falsified if the grocery-retail gap persists without any improvement in retail spending, because then trips are not converting into shopping demand.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM is at least 20 points above RETAIL_REC
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is consistently less negative than RETAIL_REC in all four weeks
failure_condition: After four weeks with GROCERY_PHARM at least 20 points above RETAIL_REC, RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to its prior 4-week mean.
